newsitem.title: UK: Schroder launches first $1.0 billion private fund.
newsitem.headline: Schroder launches first $1.0 billion private fund.

text.p: Schroder Ventures, the private equity investment arm of investment bank Schroders, on Tuesday launched Europe's first $1.0 billion private equity investment fund.

Charles Sherwood, a partner in Schroder Ventures said the fund had closed with 34 investors of whom 49 percent are from North America, 26 percent from Britain, 22 percent from continental Europe and three percent from Japan.

They include California PERS, the biggest state pension fund in the U.S.; Dutch health sector pension fund PGGM; Dutch civil service pension fund ABP; General Motors Pension Fund; U.S. insurance company Metropolitan Life; and the World Bank.

The fund, $1.023 billion, will focus on taking majority stakes in a wide spectrum of European businesses. Often they will be companies that are under performing or need a focus or investment that their current owners are unable to provide.

Peter Smitham, chairman of Schroder Ventures Europe, said the fund is talking to a number of European governments about investment in privatising businesses and will also look at family businesses seeking to develop.

"Corporations all around Europe are re-evaluating their strategies and focusing on core skills," Smitham said. "This is extremely positive, but does inevitably create an issue: What to do with non-core subsidiaries."
Sherwood said the large size of the fund will allow financing for larger deals.

"A billion dollar fund allows us to make individual long-term equity investments of $150 million," he added. "Assuming normal leverage ratios, this should enable acquisitions of $500 million and above."

Schroder said investors had been attracted by its track record which since 1985 shows a net return of 25 percent compared to a 14 percent return from comparable investments in European stock exchanges.
Investment will be for five years on average with a view to selling the business on or floating.
